subject: Customer-led storage handover & key ownership Q&A

From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@medisync.com>

Cc: Tom Park <t.park@medisync.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment - data control questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Medisync legal and security want to confirm two narrow things before we progress to procurement: 1) in a Redwood Private (VPC) deployment, can the customer fully control the encryption keys used to encrypt stored artifacts (SSTables, snapshots, backups)? 2) what evidence can you provide that stored copies were deleted (including snapshots and off-cluster backups) when the tenant leaves or requests a wipe?

High-level constraints: we are deploying to our AWS account and would prefer we bring our KMS key. We also need a short attestation that lists the deletion timeline and forensic artifacts you can hand over. Can you also flag any cross-region replication that would require additional steps?

We don’t need a full legal doc in this email — just the practical constraints and example artifacts so our infra and legal teams can evaluate scope.

Appreciate a quick turnaround; next week would be ideal.

— Sara
Security & Privacy, Medisync
[sent from iPhone]
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>

Sara — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers up front, followed by specifics and a suggested deliverable set.

Short answers:
- Yes: for Redwood Private deployed into a customer VPC we support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) for at-rest encryption; the customer key can be used for persistent store encryption and snapshots.
- Evidence of deletion: we provide a staged attestation package that includes: operation logs (snapshot deletion events + timestamps), encryption key access logs (KMS decrypt/disable events), storage lifecycle tombstone markers, and a signed verification statement from Redwood Ops.

What we’ll include in the sample handback package (attached a template):
- Timeline with timestamps (delete request received, deletion started, deletion completed)
- List of object IDs/paths removed (snapshots, backups, s3 prefixes)
- KMS access/disable audit lines (CloudTrail entries or equivalent)
- Hashes or checksums of snapshots before deletion (for chain-of-custody)
- Confirmation that replication targets were cleared (if cross-region replication enabled)

Variations / caveats:
- If you manage the KMS key in your AWS account and revoke access, Redwood’s ability to perform server-side decrypts for forensic exports is limited — we can still provide logs proving the key was disabled and storage objects were deleted, but we cannot produce plaintext artifacts encrypted under a key you control unless you grant temporary access or provide an export key.
- Backups retained by third-party backup services will require additional coordination — we will enumerate configured replication endpoints.
- Snapshots created and exported outside the VPC by your processes are considered customer-managed; Redwood will document known exports but cannot delete customer-managed artifacts outside the infra we host.

Next steps I propose:
1) Priya and Jonas will enumerate the exact audit fields we can provide from an in-VPC Private deployment.
2) We’ll populate the handback-template and return a redlineable attestation document and example CloudTrail slices.
3) If you prefer, schedule a 30-minute technical call (we can do Fri morning).

Attaching: redwood-handback-template.docx (sample deliverable) and kms-ownership-matrix.csv (summary of options).

— Markus
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Sara — adding the technical detail Priya is sending (I’m copying the exact fields our ops package can include). Quick summary then the fields:

Summary: When deployed into your AWS account our control plane runs in a customer-managed VPC (private deployment). Persistent artifacts are stored in S3 prefixes under your account (or on-prem object store) and encrypted using the KMS key you supply. We maintain a local metadata index in cluster nodes; snapshots are written to the configured object prefix. When a deletion request occurs we run an automated workflow that removes objects, rotates/evicts KV cache references, and records the sequence in an append-only audit log. We sign the attestation with a Redwoods Ops PGP key.

Audit fields we can provide (examples):
- deletion_request_id: unique id (string)
- affected_prefixes: list of s3 keys/prefixes removed
- snapshot_ids: list of snapshot uuids deleted
- deletion_started_at / deletion_completed_at: ISO timestamps
- operation_actor: service account (redwood-ops@redwoodinference.com)
- kms_key_arn: ARN of the key used to encrypt persisted objects
- kms_action_log: CloudTrail lines showing RevokeKey/DisableKey/RegisterKey operations (time + requestid + principal)
- replication_targets: list of additional regions/accounts that had copies (if present)
- tombstone_marker_hash: sha256 of tombstone manifest
- attestation_signature: base64 PGP signature string

Backups and retention notes:
- On default we keep incremental snapshots for X days (configurable per-customer). If you require immediate permanent purge we will run a forced-expunge workflow; expunge semantics include object deletion + metadata tombstone + retention purge from local node caches.
- If you bring your KMS key and disable it before the workflow runs, we will still record the attempted operations and KMS disable events (CloudTrail), but we cannot decrypt existing objects without a key. We recommend providing a temporary grant to support verification unless you prefer the auditable log-only route.

Cross-region replication:
- By default cross-region replication is off for Private (customer-controlled); we will only configure replication targets you explicitly request. If replication was enabled, the handback package will include the steps taken in each target region and confirmation logs.

Deliverable ETA: we can produce a redlineable sample attestation and a CloudTrail slice within 3 business days after you confirm the deployment region and key ARN.

— Priya
Principal Engineer, Deployment Security
Redwood Inference

Tom — thanks. We will:

1) Produce a redlineable attestation (we’ll drop an initial DocuSign-ready draft in the Drive link and send the DocuSign envelope).
2) Provide an SOW paragraph draft; proposed wording below (please redline):

"Redwood Inference will provide, upon customer request and termination of services, an attestation package describing deletion operations and supporting audit artifacts. The attestation will be signed on behalf of Redwood Inference by an authorized operations representative (Director, Operations or above) and includes timestamps, object identifiers, and cryptographic hashes of tombstone manifests. The attestation is informational evidence of Redwood's deletion workflow and does not modify the rights and obligations of the parties under the Master Services Agreement unless expressly incorporated by reference into the SOW."

3) Retention windows: default incremental snapshot retention is 30 days (configurable at contract signature to as low as 7 days or as high as 365 days). Redwood does not retain off-cluster backups beyond configured retention unless explicitly agreed (we will flag any long-term archival buckets in the Project Plan).

ETA: we will deliver the sample attestation + redlined SOW paragraph by EOD Friday (Pacific). Proposed 30 minute call on Friday 10:00am PT to walk through the package — please confirm.

Best,
— Markus
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
